answer: One of the most beautiful places I have ever been to is Sreemangal, in the tea-growing region of Sylhet, which is often called the tea capital of Bangladesh. I had been once before with my family, but I went again last winter with a couple of friends from work, and winter is the ideal time, so the scenery was absolutely [[breathtaking]]. Endless rolling hills covered in neat rows of tea bushes stretched out in every direction, glowing green in the sunlight, with tall shade trees dotted between them. In the early morning, a thin mist hung over the valleys, giving the whole place an almost [[ethereal]] quality. I remember simply standing and staring, completely [[spellbound]] by the view. Later in the day we watched the tea pickers at work, moving along the rows with baskets on their backs, and we tried the famous seven-layer tea at a little shop in town, which was as colourful as it was strange. What made it so beautiful was the untouched, [[serene]] nature of it all, so far from the traffic and dust of the roads back home. I took countless photos, but honestly none of them captured how magical it felt in person. Being in such a beautiful place had a genuinely uplifting effect on my mood, and I felt almost [[at one with]] my surroundings. It is a memory I return to whenever I need a moment of calm, and I would happily go back every winter if I could.

followUps.q: Would you like to go back there?
followUps.answer: Yes, definitely. Next time I would like to stay in one of the cottages near the forest and spend more time walking, rather than rushing around trying to see everything in a couple of days.

followUps.q: Do you prefer hills or beaches?
followUps.answer: It is a difficult choice, but probably hills. Beaches are wonderful, but places like Sreemangal feel calmer and cooler, and I love the endless shades of green and the quiet of the early morning.

note: Named the real place (Sreemangal, Sylhet) consistent with his earlier family trip; added who, tea pickers, seven-layer tea; plain 'magical' mark moved to existing 'spellbound', added 'at one with'.
